questions.explanation: [(ngModel)] is banana-in-a-box. Also in Angular 17+, model() input model for two-way.

questions.text: In Vue 3 Single File Components (SFC), what does <script setup> do?
options: It is a compile-time syntactic sugar that makes top-level bindings in <script> available in template without boilerplate setup() return
It forces the component to use Options API
It is used only for unit testing
questions.explanation: <script setup> is compile-time sugar, more concise Composition API.

questions.text: Which Angular CLI command generates a new component with standalone flag as of Angular 17+ default?
options: ng generate component my-component (standalone is now default since Angular 17)
questions.explanation: ng g c now generates standalone:true by default since Angular 17.

questions.text: In Vue, what is the purpose of v-if vs v-show?
options: v-if conditionally renders/destroys element and is lazy, v-show always renders and toggles via CSS display property
v-show removes from DOM, v-if hides with CSS
questions.explanation: v-if has higher toggle cost, v-show has higher initial render cost.

questions.text: In Angular templates, how do you iterate over a list?
options: ngFor="let item of items" (legacy) or @for (item of items; track item.id) new built-in control flow in Angular 17+
questions.explanation: Angular 17+ introduced new @for block; legacy *ngFor still valid.

questions.text: What is the default file extension for Vue Single File Components?
questions.explanation: SFCs use .vue extension containing template, script, style.

questions.text: In Vue 3, what is the difference between ref and reactive regarding unwrapping?
options: ref needs .value in JS but auto-unwraps in template; reactive cannot hold primitives and its properties are accessed directly. ref can hold any value.
questions.explanation: ref is wrapper object with .value, auto-unwrapped in templates; reactive uses Proxy.

questions.text: How do you handle a computed property with a setter in Vue 3 Composition API?
options: const fullName = computed({ get: () => first.value + ' ' + last.value, set: (val) => { [first.value, last.value] = val.split(' ') } })
questions.explanation: computed can take object with get/set for writable computed.

questions.text: In Angular, what is the new (v16+) Signals API intended to replace/improve?
options: A fine-grained reactive primitive: signal(), computed(), effect() for state, offering better change detection and interoperability than RxJS for local state and inputs
questions.explanation: Signals introduced in Angular 16 as developer preview, stable in 17, enhance reactivity and future zoneless change detection.

questions.text: Compare dependency injection in Vue vs Angular.
options: Angular has hierarchical, constructor-based DI container core to framework; Vue has Provide/Inject (provide() / inject()) which is simpler and not hierarchical in the same way, often supplemented by Pinia/composables
Angular DI only works with services
questions.explanation: Angular DI is central & hierarchical; Vue provide/inject is simpler.

questions.text: In Angular 17+, what is the purpose of defer block?
options: Deferrable views: @defer { ... } lazily loads and renders content based on triggers (viewport, idle, interaction, hover, timer), improving performance
questions.explanation: @defer is major performance feature in Angular 17 for lazy rendering.

questions.text: In Vue 3, what is Pinia and why did it replace Vuex as official recommendation in 2022?
options: Pinia is the intuitive, type-safe, Composition API-friendly store with lighter API, no mutations, devtools support, and modular stores by design
Vuex is still official, Pinia was deprecated
questions.explanation: Pinia became official in Feb 2022, Vuex 4 in maintenance. Pinia works better with TS and Composition API.

questions.text: In Angular, what is the difference between Observable and Signal as of Angular 17-18?
options: Observable is async stream (RxJS) great for events, HTTP streams, operators; Signal is synchronous reactive value with automatic dependency tracking, great for local component state. Signals can be created from observables via toSignal(), and vice versa via toObservable().
Signals are async, observables are sync
questions.explanation: Interop functions in @angular/core/rxjs-interop bridge them.

questions.text: How does Vue Router handle lazy loading vs Angular Router lazy loading (2024+)?
options: Vue: component: () => import('./View.vue'), Angular: loadComponent: () => import('./view.component').then(m => m.ViewComponent) or loadChildren for routes
questions.explanation: Both support dynamic import() for code splitting; Angular distinguishes loadComponent vs loadChildren.

questions.text: What is defineProps and defineEmits in Vue 3 <script setup>?
options: Runtime functions to import from vue router
Compiler macros (no import needed) to declare props and emits with type-based or runtime declaration, enabling type inference
They are only for Options API
questions.explanation: Compiler macros are resolved at compile time, no explicit import required.

questions.text: In Angular, what is Control Flow new syntax @if, @for, @switch vs legacy *ngIf, *ngFor, *ngSwitch?
options: New built-in control flow (Angular 17+) has better type narrowing, no need for CommonModule, better performance (no structural directive overhead), and supports @empty, @else blocks directly
questions.explanation: New control flow is recommended from Angular 17+ docs, improved DX.

questions.text: In Vue 3.4+ (2024), what major reactivity improvement was introduced with defineModel()?
options: defineModel() is a compiler macro that simplifies two-way binding for component v-model, replacing manual prop + emit pattern: const model = defineModel() returns a ref linked to prop and emits update:modelValue automatically
questions.explanation: defineModel() stable in Vue 3.4 (Jan 2024) greatly simplifies custom v-model components.

questions.text: In Angular 17-18, what is Zoneless change detection and how do Signals enable it?
options: Removing zone.js by using provideExperimentalZonelessChangeDetection() - Signals can notify Angular of changes directly without zone.js patching async APIs, reducing bundle size and improving performance
questions.explanation: Zoneless is experimental but key to Angular's future, enabled by signals. Reduces bundle by ~10kb.

questions.text: How do you implement a custom directive in Vue 3 vs Angular (advanced)?
options: Vue: app.directive('focus', { mounted(el) { el.focus() } }) with lifecycle hooks (created, mounted, updated, unmounted). Angular: @Directive({ selector: '[appHighlight]', standalone: true }) class with HostListener, ElementRef, etc.
questions.explanation: Vue directives are lightweight object with hooks; Angular directives are classes with full DI.

questions.text: In Angular, explain input() signal-based inputs (Angular 17.1+) vs decorator @Input().
options: name = input<string>('') or input.required<string>() creates Signal-based inputs: readonly signals, better type safety, input() is signal, integrates with computed/effect, supports transform functions. Replaces @Input() for new code.
questions.explanation: Signal inputs stable in Angular 17.1, enable transforms and required checks.

questions.text: Vue 3.5+ (2024) introduced useTemplateRef and Vapor mode exploration. What is Vapor mode?
options: Experimental compilation strategy that generates no virtual DOM, compiling templates to more performant direct DOM operations for significant performance gains, opt-in per component
It is the default mode since Vue 3.0
questions.explanation: Vapor mode announced 2023, progress in 2024-2025, alternative compile target for performance.

questions.text: In Angular, how do you implement SSR and hydration as of Angular 17-18?
options: ng add @angular/ssr, enables server.ts with provideClientHydration() (and with withEventReplay() in Angular 18), and hydration reuses server-rendered DOM instead of re-rendering on client to avoid flickering
questions.explanation: Angular SSR improved drastically in v17-18, hydration with event replay is major feature.

questions.text: Performance: Compare Vue's Virtual DOM optimization (Block & PatchFlag) vs Angular's new control flow and deferred loading.
options: Vue 3 compiler flags dynamic nodes with PatchFlag and creates Blocks to skip static subtrees, reducing diff cost. Angular 17+ uses new control flow that generates more efficient instructions and @defer to reduce initial bundle and JS execution.
questions.explanation: Both frameworks heavily optimized compiler output for runtime performance.

questions.text: Advanced state management: When would you use storeToRefs() in Pinia and selectSignal() / computed() in Angular with NgRx SignalStore (Angular 17-18)?
options: In Pinia, storeToRefs() preserves reactivity when destructuring store. In NgRx SignalStore, withComputed() and state as signals, store.selectSignal() or direct signal access maintains reactivity without subscribing. Both solve destructuring reactivity loss.
questions.explanation: Reactivity preservation across store patterns is crucial advanced concept.

questions.text: Testing: What are the recommended testing utilities in 2024-2026 for Vue and Angular?
options: Vue: Vue Test Utils + Vitest (Vite-native, fast), Angular: TestBed + Karma replaced by Vitest/Jest via jest-preset-angular or new experimental Vitest support, and Angular Testing Library; For E2E both recommend Playwright/Cypress
questions.explanation: Vitest dominance for Vue via Vite, Angular transitioning away from Karma (deprecated) in 2024.

questions.text: Architecturally, how would you design micro-frontends that need to mix Vue and Angular components?
options: Use Module Federation (Webpack 5 / Vite plugin), Web Components (Angular Elements createCustomElement, Vue defineCustomElement), or single-spa, with shared dependency strategy and framework-agnostic design system. Isolate change detection zones and lifecycle.
questions.explanation: Modern micro-frontend architectures enable framework interop via standards.

questions.text: What is the correct way to create a functional component in React 19?
options: class MyComp extends React.Component { render() { return <div/> } }
questions.explanation: Functional components are the standard in modern React. function MyComp() is valid.

questions.text: Which hook is used to manage local state in a functional component?
questions.explanation: useState is the primary hook for local state.

questions.text: What does JSX stand for and what happens to it during build?
options: JavaScript XML - transpiled by Babel/SWC to React.createElement() calls or JSX runtime jsx() calls
Java Syntax Extension - compiled to Java bytecode
JavaScript Extension - executed directly by browser
questions.explanation: JSX = JavaScript XML, transformed by SWC/Babel to jsx() / jsxs() runtime.

questions.text: How do you conditionally render content in React?
options: Using if statement outside JSX and ternary/logical && inside JSX
Conditional rendering is not possible in React
questions.explanation: Conditionals via if/ternary/&& are idiomatic.

questions.text: What is the purpose of the key prop when rendering lists?
options: To help React identify which items changed, added, or removed for efficient reconciliation
questions.explanation: Keys optimize reconciliation algorithm.

questions.text: In React 19, what is the default behavior for useState initial value?
options: It is always called on every render
If you pass a function, it's treated as lazy initializer and called only on initial mount
questions.explanation: Lazy initializer pattern: useState(() => expensiveCompute()) runs once.

questions.text: Which of these is the correct way to handle an onClick event?
questions.explanation: React uses camelCase onClick and function reference, not string.

questions.text: What does useEffect with an empty dependency array [] do?
options: Runs only once after initial mount (and cleanup on unmount)
questions.explanation: [] = mount only effect.

questions.text: How do you pass data from parent to child in React?
options: Props can only go from child to parent
questions.explanation: Props are unidirectional parent->child.

questions.text: What is the new feature in React 19 regarding <form> handling?
options: Native support for Actions: <form action={serverAction}> with pending state via useFormStatus
You must use controlled components only
questions.explanation: React 19 adds first-class support for Server Actions and form Actions with useFormStatus and useActionState.

questions.text: What is the difference between useEffect and useLayoutEffect?
options: useEffect runs asynchronously after paint, useLayoutEffect runs synchronously after DOM mutations but before paint, blocking visual update
questions.explanation: useLayoutEffect blocks paint; use for measurements. useEffect is non-blocking.

questions.text: In React 18+, what does useTransition do?
options: Marks a state update as non-urgent, keeping UI responsive and providing isPending flag
questions.explanation: useTransition enables concurrent rendering for non-urgent updates.

questions.text: Which statement about useMemo and useCallback is true after React Compiler (2024-2025) was introduced?
options: React Compiler auto-memoizes values and callbacks, making manual useMemo/useCallback often unnecessary in compiled components, but they remain valid API
They now work only in class components
questions.explanation: React Compiler (beta 2024, stable 2025) auto-applies memoization via Babel plugin. Manual memo still works but often redundant.

questions.text: What are React Server Components (RSC) introduced in Next.js 13+ / React 19 stable pattern?
options: Components that only run on client and use useState
Components that render on server by default, can be async, cannot use state/effects, reduce bundle size and allow direct backend data access
questions.explanation: RSC = server-only, async, zero client JS by default.

questions.text: Consider this code: const [state, formAction] = useActionState(actionFn, initialState). What does this React 19 hook do?
options: Manages form action state: takes an action function and initial state, returns current state and callable action, integrates with useFormStatus for pending/error handling
questions.explanation: useActionState (renamed from useFormState) is React 19 core for actions.

questions.text: What is the purpose of forwardRef and what is new in React 19 about refs?
options: forwardRef allowed passing refs through components; In React 19, ref is a regular prop, forwardRef is not needed - you can just do function MyComp({ref}) or receive ref as prop directly
forwardRef is required for all components now
Refs can only hold strings in React 19
questions.explanation: React 19 simplifies ref handling: ref is prop. forwardRef remains for compat but deprecated pattern.

questions.text: How does useDeferredValue differ from useTransition?
options: useDeferredValue defers the *value* (useful for debouncing search input rendering), while useTransition defers the *state update*. Both mark updates as non-urgent
questions.explanation: DeferredValue = value-based defer, Transition = update-based control.

questions.text: You have a context performance issue: every context value change re-renders all consumers even if they only use part of value. Best 2024-2026 solution?
options: Split contexts, memoize value with useMemo, or use external store like Zustand/Jotai, or use context selector pattern (proposed) / useContextSelector from third-party
questions.explanation: Context splits & memoization are standard fix; selectors pattern emerging.

questions.text: What does this React 19 code do? const data = use(fetchPromise)?
options: New use() API: can read Promise or Context conditionally unlike other hooks, suspends until promise resolves (integrates with Suspense)
questions.explanation: use() is React 19's new hook that can be called conditionally and unwraps promises/contexts.

questions.text: Why should you NOT define components inside other components?
options: On every parent render, the nested component type is new, causing React to unmount/remount the child tree, losing state and hurting performance
ESLint forbids it in React 19 compiler mode only
questions.explanation: Component identity matters - nested definitions break reconciliation.

questions.text: What is React Compiler (formerly React Forget) and how does it change optimization in 2025?
options: A build-time optimizing compiler (Babel plugin/estree) that auto-memoizes components and hooks, eliminating need for manual useMemo, useCallback, memo if components follow Rules of React, with ~2x opt-in in Next.js 15 config: experimental.reactCompiler: true
questions.explanation: Compiler auto-memoizes. Enabled via eslint-plugin-react-compiler + Next config.

questions.text: In React Server Components architecture, which hook usage causes a compile/runtime error?
options: Using useState inside a Server Component that has no "use client" directive
Using use to read a promise inside Server Component
questions.explanation: Server Components cannot use state/effects/browser APIs. Must add "use client".

questions.text: Consider hydration mismatch with {new Date().toLocaleString()} in Next.js 15. Correct 2024-2026 pattern?
options: Render date only in client via useEffect or use suppressHydrationWarning, or generate it in use promise that resolves deterministically, or use <Suspense> boundary around client-only part
questions.explanation: Date is classic hydration mismatch - must be client-only or suppressed.

questions.text: What is useOptimistic in React 19?
options: Hook to implement optimistic UI: const [optimisticState, addOptimistic] = useOptimistic(state, (curr, newVal) => ...) - shows optimistic value immediately while server action is pending, reverts if fails
questions.explanation: useOptimistic is flagship React 19 hook for optimistic updates with Actions.

questions.text: Deep dive: React 19 removes propTypes and defaultProps for function components in favor of what?
options: ES6 default parameters: function Button({ type = 'primary' }) and TypeScript/JS for typing; defaultProps removed, propTypes removed from React core (use TypeScript instead)
questions.explanation: React 19 clean-up: defaultProps for functions deprecated long ago, propTypes extracted. Use default params + TS.

questions.text: What is the correct concurrent feature pattern for data fetching in 2024-2026 React?
options: Fetch-then-render with Suspense: start fetch early (in Server Component or outside component/cache like fetch/react cache() or libraries like TanStack Query v5 + Suspense), wrap with <Suspense fallback>, use use(promise) or useSuspenseQuery, avoiding waterfall useEffect fetches
questions.explanation: Modern pattern is render-as-you-fetch with Suspense, not fetch-on-render useEffect waterfall.

questions.text: Which statement about ref cleanup function (new in React 19) is correct?
options: Ref callbacks can't return cleanup anymore
In React 19, ref callback can return a cleanup function: <div ref={(el) => { ...; return () => { cleanup } }} /> which runs when element unmounts or ref changes
questions.explanation: React 19 ref cleanup is important new feature for observers/listeners attached to DOM node.

questions.text: Advanced performance: You have const contextValue = { user, settings } recreated each render, causing child memo to fail even with React.memo. Which fixes work with React Compiler?
options: const contextValue = useMemo(() => ({user, settings}), [user, settings]) OR rely on React Compiler auto-memo if enabled and rules followed, OR split into UserContext + SettingsContext
questions.explanation: Object identity breaks memo. UseMemo or Compiler or split contexts.

questions.text: In React 19.1 (May 2025) and Next.js 15, what is the behavior of "use cache" directive?
options: New directive (React 19.1 canary) to enable per-component/request memoization caching for Server Components and Server Functions, complementing "use client" / "use server" - allows caching of async Server Component render with cacheLife and cacheTag
questions.explanation: "use cache" is emerging RSC caching primitive (Next.js 15 canary docs, React 19.1).

questions.text: Complex reconciliation question: You render <>{items.map(i=><MyComponent key={i.id} id={i.id}/>)}</> where MyComponent is memoized with React.memo. If parent re-renders but items array reference is same (e.g., from cache), and prop id unchanged, will MyComponent re-render in React 19 without compiler and with compiler?
options: Without compiler: Yes, always re-renders; With compiler: No

Without compiler: No, memo prevents re-render since props shallow-equal; With compiler: Also No, but compiler makes memo automatic even if you didn't wrap - both avoid re-render. If items array reference same but internal object mutated, still no re-render unless prop changes.
Without compiler: No, memo works; With compiler: Yes, compiler disables memo
questions.explanation: memo does shallow prop check. Same id -> no re-render. Compiler automates memo. Need stable reference & no mutation.

questions.text: What command initializes a new Git repository in your current directory?
questions.explanation: git init creates a hidden .git directory and initializes a repo.

questions.text: Which command stages a file named app.js for the next commit?
options: Both B and C are correct
questions.explanation: git add is the classic command; git stage is a synonym since Git 2.16+.

questions.text: What is the purpose of git clone <url>?
options: Creates a new branch from the remote
Downloads a copy of an existing remote repository to local
questions.explanation: Clone copies the entire remote repo including history.

questions.text: In GitHub, what is a Pull Request (PR)?
options: A request to pull the latest changes from remote to local
A proposal to merge changes from one branch into another, enabling review
An automatic backup of your repository
A command to delete a branch on GitHub
questions.explanation: PR is core GitHub collaboration workflow for code review before merging.

questions.text: What does git status show you?
options: The state of working directory and staging area, including untracked/modified files
questions.explanation: git status is your primary tool for seeing staged/unstaged/untracked changes.

questions.text: What is the .gitignore file used for?
options: To tell Git which files/folders to not track
questions.explanation: .gitignore prevents node_modules, .env, build artifacts etc. from being tracked.

questions.text: What is the difference between git fetch and git pull?
options: fetch downloads remote changes without merging, pull = fetch + merge into current branch
fetch only works with GitHub CLI
questions.explanation: Best practice: fetch first to review, then merge/pull.

questions.text: How do you create and switch to a new branch named feature-login in one command (Git 2.23+ preferred way)?
options: Both B and C work, C is the modern preferred syntax
questions.explanation: checkout -b is legacy but still works; switch -c is introduced in Git 2.23 as clearer.

questions.text: What does git commit -m "Add login page" do?
options: Saves staged changes locally with a descriptive message
Creates a new branch called "Add login page"
questions.explanation: Commit is local only; push is required to send to remote.

questions.text: On GitHub, what does forking a repository do?
options: Creates your own personal copy of someone else's repository under your account
Creates a branch in the original repository
Downloads the repo as a ZIP file
questions.explanation: Fork enables open-source contribution workflow without write access to original.

questions.text: What happens when you run git merge feature while on main?
options: It integrates commits from feature branch into main, creating a merge commit if needed
It moves main branch commits into feature
It only updates GitHub, not local
questions.explanation: Merge brings feature into current checked-out branch.

questions.text: What is the key difference between git merge and git rebase?
options: Merge keeps history non-linear with a merge commit; rebase rewrites history to create linear history
Rebase is only for remote branches
Merge rewrites history, rebase does not
questions.explanation: Merge preserves context; rebase is cleaner but rewrites history - never rebase public/shared branches.

questions.text: How do you unstage a file config.json that you accidentally added with git add?
options: Both B and C are correct (B is modern syntax, C is legacy)
questions.explanation: restore --staged is new since 2.23, reset is older but still common.

questions.text: What does git stash do?
options: Temporarily saves uncommitted changes (both staged and unstaged) so you can work on something else clean
Pushes changes to a hidden branch on GitHub
questions.explanation: Stash creates a stack; use git stash pop or apply to restore.

questions.text: How do you resolve a merge conflict?
options: Run git merge --abort and it auto-resolves
Manually edit conflicted files to remove conflict markers <<<<<<<, =======, >>>>>>>, then git add and git commit
questions.explanation: Conflicts require manual resolution. Tools like VS Code help, but markers must be resolved.

questions.text: What is git cherry-pick <commit-hash> used for?
options: To apply the changes from a specific commit from one branch onto current branch
To view details of a commit
questions.explanation: Cherry-pick is useful for hotfixes - picking one commit without merging whole branch.

questions.text: On GitHub, what are Protected Branch rules (as of 2024-2026)?
options: Rules to prevent force pushes and require PR reviews/status checks before merging to main
Rules to make a branch private
Rules to hide branches from contributors
questions.explanation: Introduced to enforce team quality gates: required reviews, CI passing, no force push on main.

questions.text: What does git log --oneline --graph --all show?
options: A compact visual graph of all branches and commits history
questions.explanation: Essential for understanding branching structure; --all shows all branches.

questions.text: What file defines GitHub Actions workflows?
questions.explanation: GitHub Actions workflows live in that directory and run on push/PR/schedule.

questions.text: How do you undo the last commit but keep its changes staged, to edit the commit message or add more files?
questions.explanation: --soft moves HEAD but keeps index and working dir. --hard deletes changes, --mixed (default) unstages.

questions.text: What is git reflog and when would you use it?
options: Log of remote fetches; used for performance tracking
A log of all moves of HEAD in local repo (commits, resets, rebases, merges) - crucial for recovering lost commits after reset --hard or deleted branches
questions.explanation: Reflog is local only, not pushed, lasts 90 days by default. Essential recovery tool.

questions.text: What does git bisect do?
options: Uses binary search to find the commit that introduced a bug by testing commits between good and bad
questions.explanation: git bisect start, bisect bad, bisect good <hash>, then test and mark good/bad until culprit found. Automatable with git bisect run <script>.

questions.text: As of GitHub 2024, what is the purpose of CODEOWNERS file?
options: To list who pays for GitHub
To automatically request reviews from specific teams/individuals when files they own are changed in a PR
To prevent anyone from cloning the repo
questions.explanation: Located at .github/CODEOWNERS or root/docs; enables auto-review assignment and can be required by branch protection.

questions.text: Consider you accidentally ran git reset --hard HEAD~3 and lost 3 commits. They are not pushed. How to recover most reliably?
options: git push --force to restore from GitHub
Use git reflog to find the hash before reset, then git reset --hard <hash> or git branch recovery <hash>
questions.explanation: Reflog contains HEAD~ before reset. This is why resetting shared branches is dangerous but locally recoverable.

questions.text: What is the difference between git revert <commit> and git reset?
options: Revert creates a new commit that undoes changes of an old commit (safe for public history), reset moves branch pointer backwards and rewrites history (unsafe for pushed branches)
questions.explanation: Revert is safe for collaborative work. Reset + force push should be limited to private feature branches.

questions.text: What are Git Submodules vs Git Subtree (2024-2026 best practice)?
options: Submodules link a specific commit of another repo inside parent (keeps separate history but complex), Subtree merges external repo code into parent repo history (simpler for contributors)
Submodules copy code, Subtree only links
questions.explanation: 2024-2026: Many teams prefer Subtree or package manager over Submodules due to UX complexity. Monorepo tools often replace both.

questions.text: In GitHub Actions, what is the difference between GITHUB_TOKEN and a Personal Access Token (PAT) for permissions?
options: GITHUB_TOKEN is auto-generated per workflow run, scoped to current repo, expires after job; PAT is user-generated, longer-lived, can span multiple repos/orgs but must be managed manually - GITHUB_TOKEN is preferred for 2024+ due to fine-grained PATs

questions.text: How does Git internally store data?
options: As a content-addressable filesystem with objects: blob (file content), tree (directory), commit (metadata + pointer to tree + parent), and tag - all identified by SHA-1 (and SHA-256 support from Git 2.29+ experimental)
questions.explanation: Git snapshots, not deltas (though packfiles use deltas for storage efficiency). Blobs store content, SHA-1 hashes content.

questions.text: What does this GitHub Pull Request Merge Strategy do: "Squash and merge"?
options: Creates a merge commit with all commits preserved
Combines all PR commits into a single commit on base branch, producing linear history but losing granular PR commit history
Rebases all commits one by one
questions.explanation: 3 GitHub strategies: Merge commit, Squash, Rebase and merge. Squash common for feature branches to keep main linear and clean.

questions.text: You need to keep a secret .env file that was committed and pushed 10 commits ago out of GitHub history completely (due to leaked API key). What is the correct modern approach (2024-2026)?
options: Just add to .gitignore and commit deletion

Use git filter-repo (or BFG Repo Cleaner) or GitHub's git filter-repo / git-filter-repo to rewrite history removing that file from all commits, then force push, and rotate the leaked secret immediately. Also use GitHub's secret push protection.

questions.text: What does the management plugin provide?
options: HTTP API and web UI on port 15672 for monitoring and administration

questions.text: In RabbitMQ, what is a Binding?
options: A connection between consumer and producer
A link between an exchange and a queue defining routing rules

questions.text: Which protocol does RabbitMQ support natively for IoT use cases via plugin?

It is broadcast to all queues

questions.text: What is Redis commonly used for?
questions.explanation: Redis is an in-memory data store often used for caching, queues, and fast lookups.

questions.text: What does TTL mean in Redis?
questions.explanation: TTL specifies how long a key remains before expiration.

questions.text: Which Redis structure stores field-value pairs under one key?
questions.explanation: A Redis hash stores multiple field-value pairs associated with a key.

questions.text: Why use cache-aside?
options: The application loads missing data into cache on demand
The cache writes every DB change automatically
questions.explanation: Cache-aside lets the application read the database on a miss and populate the cache.

questions.text: What is cache stampede?
options: Many requests simultaneously recompute an expired value
questions.explanation: A stampede occurs when many clients miss the same cache entry and overload the backend.

options: Tracking managed resources and their attributes
questions.explanation: State maps configuration resources to real infrastructure objects.

questions.text: What does `terraform plan` do?
questions.explanation: `plan` calculates and displays the intended infrastructure changes.

questions.text: What does `terraform apply` do?
questions.explanation: `apply` executes the proposed changes against configured providers.

options: To coordinate shared state and prevent concurrent updates
questions.explanation: Remote state centralizes state and locking helps prevent conflicting operations.
